sop_title: FCC Government Purchase Card Program Directive: Purchase Card Procedures (Sections 6, 7, 8, 11-14)
summary: This SOP covers how FCC purchase cards are issued and how limits are changed. It also covers how purchases are authorized and made, how monthly statements of account (SOAs) are reconciled and certified, and how disputes, lost cards, reviews, misuse and departures are handled. It is run by cardholders, Approving Officials (AOs), Bureau/Office Chiefs, the Agency Program Coordinator (APC) and the Financial Operations Center (FOC) under the CFO, with the contractor bank, EAC, OIG and Human Resources involved at specific points.

sections.title: General: issuance to FTEs and Single Purchase Limit
sections.reason: Its statements about eligibility, merchant controls and the SPL could be reordered without loss of meaning; it supplies the trigger and eligibility gate for card issuance.

sections.title: General: offices not eligible for cards
sections.reason: It is a reorderable list of ineligible and eligible offices that gates nomination (D1).

sections.title: General: Form A-498 nomination form
sections.reason: Its two requirements (complete/sign and certify) can be swapped; it gates issuance as a 'prior to issuance' condition (S3, D2).

sections.title: General: GSA training and refresher training
sections.reason: Its training requirements could be listed in any order; they gate issuance and drive the refresher process.

sections.title: General: inactive account review
sections.reason: Order matters: the APC reviews usage, then sends a list, then the Bureau/Office confirms, and suspension follows only if no confirmation is given.

sections.title: General: card as preferred procurement method
sections.reason: It is a single policy preference with no position in the flow.

sections.title: General: state sales tax exemption
sections.reason: It sets ordered conditional actions: check the exemption at the point of sale, decline if refused, and seek a credit if tax was charged.

sections.title: General: prohibited terms and conditions; EAC referral
sections.reason: Order matters: terms are reviewed before purchase and referred to EAC before any commitment, and only then does EAC contract.

sections.title: General: price reasonableness
sections.reason: It is a single condition that gates the purchase (D10).

sections.title: General: premium shipping discouraged
sections.reason: It is a reorderable set of cautions; it is recorded as an exception on the purchase step.

sections.title: General: no requisition required
sections.reason: It is a standalone policy statement with no position in the cardholder flow.

sections.title: General: mandatory Government sources (FAR Part 8)
sections.reason: It is a requirement whose wording ('only after the priority sources have been considered') places a source check before purchase (S21).

sections.title: Single transaction limit: default, EAC contracting officers, increases
sections.reason: The increase path is ordered (AO written request and justification, then APC grant), and the EAC limit is set at the time of the initial application.

sections.title: Single transaction limit not to be exceeded
sections.reason: It is a single limit that gates the purchase (D10).

sections.title: Monthly credit limit: default and EAC contracting officers
sections.reason: It contains reorderable limit statements; the AO's determination for EAC contracting officers is mapped at issuance (S9).

sections.title: Monthly credit limit increase via Form A-1204
sections.reason: Order matters: the AO submits Form A-1204, then the APC grants the increase and retains the justification.

sections.title: Periodic review of permanent credit limit increases
sections.reason: It describes a recurring review action by the APC with its own trigger and outcome, mapped as its own short process.

sections.title: Reconciliation: cardholder reconciles and forwards SOA
sections.reason: The cardholder must reconcile, then sign, then forward; reversing that would break the meaning.

sections.title: Reconciliation: AO review and forwarding to FOC
sections.reason: The AO reviews, then signs, then forwards to FOC RDG/TOG in that order.

sections.title: Reconciliation: signature of accepting employee
sections.reason: It requires the other employee's signature before reconciliation ('may not reconcile ... until').

sections.title: Certification Clause for reconciled SOAs
sections.reason: Its four certified items could be reordered; the instruction to note exceptions becomes branches on the signing steps.

sections.title: Records Retention
sections.reason: It is a reorderable list of required supporting documents; it is mapped as the retention step and as exceptions.

sections.title: Cardholder Review: subject to reviews and audits
sections.reason: It is a statement of reviewer authority and a compliance duty; it supplies the trigger for the review process.

sections.title: Cardholder Review: furnishing documents to reviewers
sections.reason: Upon a review request, the cardholder furnishes the documents directly; this response is positioned after the request.

sections.title: Responsibilities: Managing Director
sections.reason: It states agency-level authority only.

sections.title: Responsibilities: Chief Financial Officer
sections.reason: It is a reorderable list of CFO duties; data entry and bank payment are tied to receipt of reconciled SOAs and are mapped (S39, S40).

sections.title: Responsibilities: Bureau and Office Chiefs
sections.reason: It is a reorderable list of duties; only nominating (issuance) and reporting status changes (separation) have a position in the flow.

sections.title: Responsibilities: Agency Program Coordinator
sections.reason: It is a reorderable list of APC duties; issuing cards and closing accounts are tied to issuance and separation.

sections.title: Responsibilities: Approving Official
sections.reason: It is a reorderable list; items worded 'before the purchase is made', 'within ten (10) workdays' and 'leaving the Commission' are mapped to their points in the flow.

sections.title: Responsibilities: Cardholder
sections.reason: It is a reorderable list; items tied to the flow ('before making the purchase', 'prior to initiating', 'within seven (7) workdays', 'upon leaving') are mapped.

sections.title: Span of Control for APCs and AOs
sections.reason: It is a management control statement with no position in any flow.

sections.title: Consequences of abuse, misuse and non-compliance
sections.reason: Its sequence matters: suspension until compliance, refresher training before restoration, reporting to the AO, and permanent closure on repeat instances.

sections.title: Criminal, Disciplinary, and Adverse Actions
sections.reason: It is a reorderable list of possible consequences; its permanent-closure rule is cited on S59.

sections.title: Personal liability for intentional misuse
sections.reason: It is a reorderable list of liabilities with no position in the flow.

sections.title: APC reporting of misuse or fraud
sections.reason: The APC reports to the supervisor, HR and OIG for investigation, and any proposed action then follows the HR progression.

sections.title: Disputing a Charge: dispute steps
sections.reason: Its numbered steps (review receipts, contact merchant, then dispute with the bank) must happen in order.

sections.title: Disputing a Charge: shipping and tax charges
sections.reason: It is a single rule that gates escalation to the bank (D18).

sections.title: Card Security
sections.reason: The lost or stolen card report is an event-triggered action sequence (report to the bank, notify the AO and APC); the safekeeping text is rules.

sections.title: Separation or Transfer: Cardholder
sections.reason: Prior notice, handover of records and card before separation, and the AO note on the final SOA are positioned in time.

sections.title: Separation or Transfer: AO
sections.reason: The new AO is designated, then the designation is sent in writing to the APC.

sections.title: Separation or Transfer: APC
sections.reason: The APC closes the account upon being notified, which fixes its position after notification.

processes.name: Issue a purchase card
processes.trigger: Bureau/Office Chief, Designee, or the employee's manager requests a card for an FCC full-time employee
processes.outcome: Card issued and account opened by the APC with the applicable limits

processes.name: Increase a single transaction limit
processes.trigger: A cardholder other than an EAC contracting officer has a demonstrated need for a higher single transaction limit
processes.outcome: Single transaction limit permanently increased up to the MPT, or the request is not granted

processes.name: Increase a monthly credit limit
processes.trigger: A cardholder needs a higher monthly credit limit
processes.outcome: Monthly credit limit increased (temporary or permanent) with the circumstances retained by the APC

processes.name: Review permanent credit limit increases
processes.trigger: Periodic review cycle set by the APC
processes.outcome: Determination of whether each permanent higher limit is still required

processes.name: Make a purchase
processes.trigger: Cardholder has a requirement for supplies or services
processes.outcome: Authorized purchase made tax-exempt and receipt validated, or the requirement referred to EAC for a contract

processes.name: Reconcile the monthly statement
processes.trigger: End of the billing cycle and receipt of the monthly SOA from the contractor bank
processes.outcome: SOA reconciled and certified by cardholder and AO, recorded and paid by FOC, with documentation retained

processes.name: Dispute a charge
processes.trigger: Cardholder identifies a questionable transaction on the SOA
processes.outcome: Charge resolved with the merchant, or a dispute is filed with the contractor bank and tracked to completion

processes.name: Report a lost or stolen card
processes.trigger: Purchase card is lost or stolen
processes.outcome: Contractor bank, AO and APC notified

processes.name: Complete refresher training
processes.trigger: Three years since the last training, or direction from the APC
processes.outcome: Refresher training certificate provided to the APC

processes.name: Review inactive accounts
processes.outcome: Continued need confirmed for each inactive account, or the account is suspended until confirmation

processes.name: Respond to a purchase card review or audit
processes.trigger: APC, independent auditors, OIG or another federal entity selects cardholder transactions for review
processes.outcome: Documentation furnished to the reviewer, or the cardholder's standing reviewed by the APC

processes.name: Handle misuse or non-compliance
processes.trigger: APC identifies purchase card abuse, misuse, fraud or non-compliance
processes.outcome: Privileges suspended and restored, or permanently closed, with misuse or fraud referred to OIG and HR

processes.name: Separate or transfer a cardholder
processes.trigger: Cardholder is transferring within the agency or separating from the agency
processes.outcome: Records and card handed over, account closed, and final SOA annotated if needed

processes.name: Replace a separating AO
processes.outcome: New AO designated and the designation sent in writing to the APC

steps.actor: Bureau/Office Chief (or Designee or employee's manager)
steps.action: Requests a purchase card for the employee and nominates the cardholder and AO
steps.input: Employee's need for a purchase card
steps.source_quote: The FCC issues Purchase Cards only to FCC Full-Time Employees(FTEs) upon request

steps.source_quote: must complete the General Services Administration (GSA) purchase card web-based training prior to issuance of the purchase card

steps.action: Completes and signs Form A-498, certifying that the directive has been read and understood

steps.action: Signs the cardholder nominee's Form A-498
steps.source_quote: signed by their Bureau/Office Chief (or Assistant Bureau Chief (ABC) for Management if applicable) and their AO

steps.action: Signs the cardholder nominee's Form A-498
steps.source_quote: signed by their Bureau/Office Chief (or Assistant Bureau Chief (ABC) for Management if applicable) and their AO

steps.action: Submits the AO's training certificate of completion to the APC
steps.output: AO training certificate on file with the APC
steps.source_quote: Submit a certificate of completion of cardholder training (the same training required of purchase cardholder nominees) to the APC

steps.action: Submits the bank card application form, training certificate and signed Form A-498 to FOC RDG/TOG
steps.input: Bank card application form, training certificate, signed Form A-498
steps.source_quote: submit a completed bank card application form to FOC, RDG/TOG for submission to the contractor bank

steps.action: Submits the bank card application to the contractor bank
steps.source_quote: for submission to the contractor bank

steps.action: Determines the monthly credit limit for an EAC contracting officer whose single transaction limit (set no higher than warrant authority) exceeds the MPT
steps.input: Contracting officer's warrant authority and single transaction limit
steps.source_quote: will be granted a monthly credit limit at an amount determined by their AO to reasonably accommodate their higher single transaction limit

steps.action: Issues the card and opens the account with the default $15,000 single transaction and monthly limits, or the approved higher limits
steps.input: Approved application, training certificate, Form A-498
steps.output: Issued purchase card and open account
steps.source_quote: issues and destroys cards; opens and closes accounts

steps.action: Submits a written request and justification of the cardholder's demonstrated need to the APC
steps.source_quote: upon written request and justification provided by the respective cardholder

steps.action: Reviews the request case by case
steps.source_quote: may be granted a single transaction limit up to the MPT on a case-by-case basis

steps.action: Permanently increases the cardholder's single transaction limit up to the MPT
steps.source_quote: may grant a permanent increase of the single transaction limit up to the MPT

steps.action: Submits FCC Form A-1204 Request for Monthly Credit Limit Increase to the APC
steps.input: Cardholder need for a higher monthly limit
steps.source_quote: Submit a written request via FCC Form A-1204 Request for Monthly Credit Limit Increase to the APC

steps.action: Increases the cardholder's monthly credit limit on a temporary or permanent basis
steps.source_quote: monthly credit limit may be increased by the APC upon written request

steps.action: Retains the circumstances for the increase and its duration
steps.source_quote: shall be retained by the APC

steps.action: Reviews permanent monthly credit limit increases to determine whether the higher limits are still required
steps.source_quote: Permanent monthly credit limit increases shall be reviewed by the APC on a periodic basis

steps.action: Requests written authorization from the AO for the purchase
steps.source_quote: Obtain written authorization from the AO for each purchase before making the purchase

steps.action: Provides written authorization for the transaction to the cardholder
steps.source_quote: Provide written authorization (such as through a memo, note, or e-mail) to the cardholder for each purchase card transaction before the purchase is made

steps.action: Ensures funds are available for the purchase
steps.source_quote: Ensure availability of funds prior to initiating a purchase with the card

steps.action: Considers mandatory Government priority sources under FAR Part 8 before other sources and selects a merchant, directing questions to EAC
steps.source_quote: Other sources may be considered for use only after the priority sources have been considered

steps.action: Completes and attaches the Section 508 Determination and Findings for Purchase Requests Form
steps.input: IT product or service covered by accessibility regulations
steps.system: Section 508 Determination and Findings for Purchase Requests Form
steps.source_quote: Complete and attach Section 508 Determination and Findings for Purchase Requests Form if the item is covered by the accessibility regulations

steps.action: Considers the price of the goods or services and checks it against the single transaction limit
steps.source_quote: Cardholders must consider the price of goods or services being purchased

steps.action: Reviews the vendor's terms and conditions for prohibited provisions
steps.source_quote: Cardholders are responsible for reviewing terms and conditions applicable to any purchase before making the purchase

steps.action: Refers the agreement with prohibited provisions (or an indemnification clause) to EAC before making any commitment
steps.source_quote: Cardholders shall refer all agreements that include such provisions to the Enterprise Acquisition Center (EAC) prior to making any commitment on behalf of the Government

steps.action: Establishes a contract that addresses the objectionable terms, consulting OGC as necessary
steps.source_quote: so that EAC can establish a contract that addresses the objectionable terms

steps.action: Makes the purchase with the card and ensures the state sales tax exemption is applied at the point of sale
steps.source_quote: Cardholders should ensure that their purchases have been exempted from state sales tax at the point of sale

steps.action: Declines the purchase and seeks a merchant who will honor the tax exemption
steps.source_quote: the cardholder shall not make the purchase and should instead seek a merchant who will honor the exemption

steps.action: Validates receipt of the purchased items and signs the receipt or invoice received with the shipment
steps.source_quote: Validate the receipt of items purchased, as applicable

steps.action: Contacts the merchant to seek a credit for the charged sales tax and documents the effort
steps.output: Credit request and documentation of efforts
steps.source_quote: cardholders are responsible for contacting the merchant to seek a credit for the charged sales tax

steps.action: Issues the monthly SOA to the cardholder
steps.source_quote: monthly SOA received from the contractor bank

steps.action: Obtains the signature and date of the employee who accepted or first used the goods or services on the invoice
steps.output: Invoice signed and dated by the accepting employee
steps.source_quote: the cardholder may not reconcile his/her SOA until they have obtained the signature and date of that other employee on the invoice

steps.action: Reconciles the SOA against receipts, invoices and supporting documentation
steps.source_quote: Cardholders shall reconcile their monthly SOA received from the contractor bank within seven (7) workdays after the end of the billing cycle

steps.action: Notes exceptions to the Certification Clause on the SOA and initials and dates the remarks
steps.source_quote: Any exceptions to the Certification Clause must be noted on the SOA by the cardholder or AO, with the remarks being initialed and dated

steps.action: Signs, dates and prints name on the reconciled SOA and forwards it to the AO
steps.output: Cardholder-certified SOA sent to the AO
steps.source_quote: the cardholder must affix a dated signature and printed name on the reconciled SOA and forward it to his/her AO for review

steps.action: Reviews the reconciled SOA to verify that all transactions were legal, proper, correct and necessary
steps.source_quote: AOs shall review each reconciled SOA received from their purchase cardholders within ten (10) workdays after the end of the billing cycle

steps.action: Notes exceptions to the Certification Clause on the SOA and initials and dates the remarks
steps.source_quote: Any exceptions to the Certification Clause must be noted on the SOA by the cardholder or AO, with the remarks being initialed and dated

steps.action: Signs, dates and prints name on the reconciled SOA and forwards it to FOC RDG/TOG
steps.source_quote: The AO then must forward the reconciled SOA to Financial Operations Center (FOC), Revenue and Disbursement Group (RDG)/Travel and Operations Group (TOG)

steps.action: Ensures the reconciled transaction data is entered into the core financial accounting system and charges are distributed to the correct accounts
steps.source_quote: ensuring all reconciled purchase card transaction data is entered into the Commission

steps.action: Pays the purchase card contractor bank
steps.source_quote: for paying the purchase card contractor bank

steps.action: Retains copies of the reconciled SOA and all supporting documentation for six years
steps.source_quote: Retain copies of each reconciled SOA, as well as all supporting documentation for purchase transactions for a period of six (6) years after final payment

steps.action: Reviews the receipts for the questioned transaction
steps.source_quote: Review the receipts. For example, the transaction in question may have posted to the SOA with a different merchant name.

steps.action: Contacts the merchant to try to resolve the disputed charge and documents the actions taken
steps.source_quote: the cardholder shall contact the merchant in an attempt to resolve the disputed charge. Cardholders shall document the actions taken to resolve the issue.

steps.action: Initiates a dispute request with the purchase card contractor bank
steps.output: Dispute filed with the contractor bank
steps.source_quote: If unable to resolve the dispute with the merchant, the cardholder shall immediately proceed with a dispute request with the purchase card contractor bank.

steps.action: Tracks the dispute to completion
steps.source_quote: Cardholders shall track disputes to completion.

steps.process: Report a lost or stolen card
steps.action: Reports the lost or stolen card to the purchase card contractor bank
steps.source_quote: The cardholder shall immediately report lost or stolen purchase cards to the purchase card contractor bank

steps.process: Report a lost or stolen card
steps.action: Notifies the AO and the APC of the lost or stolen card
steps.source_quote: and notify both the AO and the APC

steps.action: Completes the GSA web-based refresher training
steps.source_quote: as refresher training every three (3) years or as directed by the APC

steps.action: Provides certification of the refresher training to the APC
steps.output: Certificate on file with the APC
steps.source_quote: and to provide certification of training to the APC

steps.action: Reviews purchase card usage to identify accounts with no activity in the preceding three years
steps.source_quote: the APC will review purchase card usage to identify inactive accounts

steps.action: Provides the list of inactive accounts to each Bureau/Office
steps.source_quote: The APC will provide a list of inactive accounts to each Bureau/Office

steps.action: Confirms the continued need for each inactive account
steps.source_quote: the Bureau/Office must confirm the continued need for each inactive account

steps.action: Suspends the inactive account until confirmation is received
steps.source_quote: suspension until confirmation is received

steps.process: Respond to a purchase card review or audit
steps.actor: Reviewer (APC, independent auditors, OIG, or other federal entity)
steps.action: Selects the cardholder's transactions for periodic or random review and requests the supporting documentation
steps.source_quote: Cardholders shall be subject to periodic and/or random reviews of their purchase card transactions and purchase practices by the APC

steps.process: Respond to a purchase card review or audit
steps.action: Furnishes copies of the reconciled SOAs and all supporting documentation directly to the reviewer
steps.source_quote: cardholders are directly responsible for furnishing copies of their reconciled SOAs and all other supporting documentation

steps.process: Respond to a purchase card review or audit
steps.action: Reviews the cardholder's standing in the program, which may result in temporary suspension or expulsion
steps.source_quote: will be subject to review by the APC. Such review may, among other appropriate actions, result in temporary suspension

steps.action: Temporarily suspends card privileges or revokes AO authority until compliance is observed
steps.output: Suspended privileges or revoked AO authority
steps.source_quote: may result in temporary suspension of card privileges or revocation of AO authority by the APC until compliance is observed

steps.action: Reports the abuse, misuse or non-compliance to the cardholder's AO or the AO's immediate supervisor
steps.output: Report to the AO or supervisor
steps.source_quote: will report purchase card abuse, misuse, and non-compliance

steps.action: Permanently closes the purchase card privileges or revokes AO authority
steps.input: Repeated non-compliance, or misuse or fraud
steps.output: Permanently closed privileges or revoked authority
steps.source_quote: Repeated instances of abuse, misuse, or non-compliance will result in permanent closure of purchase card privileges or revocation of AO authority

steps.action: Reports the misuse or fraud to the immediate supervisor (or ABC), the Chief of HRM Labor Relations and Performance Management, and the OIG
steps.output: Referral to supervisor, HR and OIG
steps.source_quote: the Chief of Human Resources Management Labor Relations and Performance Management, and the OIG for investigation and appropriate actions

steps.action: Investigates the reported misuse or fraud
steps.source_quote: the OIG for investigation and appropriate actions

steps.action: Processes the proposed disciplinary or adverse action under the Basic Negotiated Agreement or the FCC Personnel Manual
steps.source_quote: these actions will follow the normal progression through Human Resources

steps.action: Completes refresher training when required by the APC before restoration
steps.source_quote: The APC may also require the cardholder or AO to complete refresher training before restoring card privileges or AO authority.

steps.action: Restores card privileges or AO authority once compliance is observed
steps.input: Observed compliance and any required refresher training
steps.source_quote: before restoring card privileges or AO authority

steps.action: Notifies the APC of the reassignment or departure
steps.source_quote: Prior to reassignment to another FCC organization or upon leaving the agency, notify the APC

steps.action: Gives the APC prior written notice of the transfer or separation and directs cancellation of the card
steps.output: Written notice/cancellation direction to the APC
steps.source_quote: prior notice shall be given to the APC

steps.action: Provides all purchase card records and supporting documentation to the AO
steps.source_quote: provide all of their purchase card records and supporting documentation to their AO

steps.action: Surrenders the purchase card to the AO or the APC
steps.source_quote: surrender their purchase card to their AO or the APC

steps.action: Closes the cardholder's account
steps.output: Closed account and cancelled procurement authority
steps.source_quote: the APC shall close the cardholder's account

steps.action: Notes on the final reconciled SOA that the departed cardholder could not sign and date it
steps.source_quote: the AO shall note this on the cardholder's final reconciled SOA

steps.action: Designates a new AO to assume the duties of the previous AO
steps.source_quote: a new AO will be designated by the appropriate Bureau/Office Chief (or ABC if applicable)

steps.action: Sends the change in AO designation in writing to the APC
steps.source_quote: This change in official designation shall be sent in writing to the APC.

Reviewer (APC, independent auditors, OIG, or other federal entity)

exceptions.trigger: Nominee works in FOC, OCH or a Commissioner's office, or is not a full-time employee
exceptions.handling: The FCC does not issue a card; no next step or notification is stated.

exceptions.trigger: Contractor bank rejects or delays the card application
Card is used without first ensuring funds are available
exceptions.handling: This may result in an Anti-Deficiency Act violation; no corrective step is stated.

exceptions.trigger: Employee discovers an indemnification provision in any vendor agreement
exceptions.handling: Consult EAC to determine whether the FAR regulation applies or whether to forgo the vendor.

exceptions.trigger: Merchant refuses the state sales tax exemption at the point of sale
exceptions.handling: Do not make the purchase; seek a merchant who will honor the exemption.

exceptions.trigger: Repeated use of premium shipping or rush delivery
exceptions.handling: This may be deemed charge card abuse by the APC and could lead to administrative action.

exceptions.trigger: State sales tax inadvertently charged
exceptions.handling: Cardholder contacts the merchant for a credit and documents the effort; tax charges are not disputable with the bank.

exceptions.trigger: Transaction posted under a third-party payment processor name (e.g., PayPal) instead of the merchant
exceptions.handling: Maintain documentation of the merchant, merchant contact, processor name, amount and justification for using that merchant.

exceptions.trigger: Cardholder misses the 7-workday reconciliation deadline
exceptions.handling: Untimely statement reconciliation may result in temporary suspension of card privileges by the APC.

exceptions.trigger: AO finds a transaction that is not legal, proper, correct or necessary
exceptions.handling: The exception must be noted on the SOA, initialed and dated; what happens to the improper charge is not stated.

exceptions.trigger: AO does not forward the reconciled SOA within 10 workdays
Cardholder's SOA is missing or supporting documentation is lacking
exceptions.handling: The APC reviews the cardholder's standing, which may result in temporary suspension or expulsion from the program.

exceptions.trigger: Cardholder must retain a copy of the SOA signed by both cardholder and AO, but the signed SOA is forwarded by the AO to FOC
Dispute not initiated with the bank within 90 calendar days of the charge first appearing on the SOA
exceptions.handling: Failure to dispute in time can result in administrative and/or disciplinary or adverse action.

exceptions.trigger: Disputed charge is a shipping or tax charge
exceptions.handling: Not disputable with the bank; the cardholder is responsible for obtaining a credit from the merchant.

exceptions.trigger: Contractor bank denies the dispute
Card reported lost or stolen
Bureau/Office indicates an inactive account is no longer needed
Bureau/Office fails to confirm continued need for an inactive account
exceptions.handling: The account is suspended until confirmation is received.

exceptions.trigger: Cardholder forwards the review request to a third party or refers the reviewer to a central source
exceptions.handling: Not permitted; the cardholder remains directly responsible for furnishing the documentation.

exceptions.trigger: Cardholder transfers or separates before the final SOA is available and cannot sign it
exceptions.handling: The AO notes this on the cardholder's final reconciled SOA.

timing.requirement: Training must be completed prior to issuance of the card or certification as an AO.
Form A-498 must be completed and signed prior to issuance of the card or certification as an AO.
The training certificate must be submitted prior to issuance; cardholders may not make purchases until training is complete.
Permanent monthly credit limit increases are reviewed on a periodic basis (no interval stated).
Written authorization must be given before the purchase is made.
Funds availability must be confirmed prior to initiating the purchase.
Terms must be reviewed before making the purchase.
The referral to EAC must occur prior to making any commitment on behalf of the Government.
AO validates receipt 'prior to the cardholder's receipt' (as written).
The accepting employee's signature must be obtained before the cardholder may reconcile the SOA.
Reconcile within seven (7) workdays after the end of the billing cycle.
AO review within ten (10) workdays after the end of the billing cycle.
The CFO ensures timely receipt of reconciled SOAs from AOs (no period stated).
Retain documentation for six (6) years after final payment (6.D states six years without the 'after final payment' anchor).
Proceed immediately when merchant resolution fails, and in any event within 90 calendar days from the date the charge first appeared on the SOA.
Report the lost or stolen card immediately.
Notify the AO and APC immediately.
Refresher training every three (3) years or as directed by the APC.
Coincides with each agency-wide refresher training initiative; an account is inactive after no activity in the preceding three (3) years.
Provide documentation in a timely manner (no period stated).
Suspension lasts until compliance is observed.
Notify the APC prior to reassignment or upon leaving the agency.
Prior notice must be given to the APC before the transfer or separation.
Promptly, and before separation or transfer.
Promptly, and before separation or transfer.
Upon being notified of the transfer or separation.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The cardholder's request and the AO's authorization move by memo, note or email with no tracking. A purchase can be made before authorization arrives, or the authorization cannot be found when an auditor asks for it.
risks.cause: 7.E.2 and 7.F.4 accept 'a memo, note, or email' as written authorization, and 6.D requires a copy of the advance authorization in the purchase file. No log or standard format is stated.
risks.impact: Unauthorized commitments, audit findings for missing authorization, and possible suspension of the cardholder under 6.D or 11.B.

quantified_impact.basis: Map handoffs after S18 (Cardholder to AO) and S19 (AO to Cardholder)

risks.severity_reason: This runs for every purchase with no system record, and a missing advance authorization is a direct audit and misuse finding.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: When the AO declines, funds are not available, or the price is unreasonable or over the single transaction limit, the SOP does not say what the cardholder does next. Requests stall or are retried informally.
risks.cause: The 'No' branches of D7 (7.E.2/7.F.4), D8 (7.F.5) and D10 (6.A.9, 6.B.2) have no stated next step.
risks.impact: Requesters get delayed or inconsistent outcomes, and workarounds such as splitting a requirement become more likely.

quantified_impact.metric: Decision branches with no next step
quantified_impact.basis: D7, D8 and D10 'No' branches are UNDEFINED in the map

risks.severity_reason: Declines and limit breaches happen regularly, but the harm is mostly delay unless a workaround is used.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A cardholder splits one requirement into several charges to stay under the single transaction limit, and nobody notices until a later review.
risks.cause: S23 relies only on the cardholder checking the limit (6.B.2). 11.B names 'splitting a purchase requirement' as non-compliance, but no step before the purchase detects it.
risks.impact: Limit circumvention and possible procurement rule violations, found only after the money is spent.
risks.severity_reason: It is moderately likely because the check is self-applied, and it is a compliance breach once it occurs.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A cardholder accepts online terms that contain automatic renewal, recurring payments or indemnification without spotting them, so the agency is bound to open-ended liability.
risks.cause: 6.A.8 leaves the review of terms to the cardholder alone before purchase. The referral to EAC depends on the cardholder recognizing the provision.
risks.impact: Possible fiscal law or Anti-Deficiency Act exposure and unplanned recurring charges.

quantified_impact.basis: 6.A.8 lists recurring payments, automatic renewal, unlimited duration, indemnification, and unlimited liability terms

risks.severity_reason: Vendor terms are long and easy to miss, and the impact is legal and fiscal.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: No one is sure who signs for receipt of goods: the AO, the accepting employee, or the purchaser. Invoices reach reconciliation without the required signature.
risks.cause: 7.E.3 has the AO validate receipt 'prior to the cardholder's receipt' and sign the invoice. 6.C.3 requires the accepting employee's signature. 6.D requires the invoice signed by the purchaser if other than the cardholder.
risks.impact: Incomplete supporting documentation, delayed reconciliation, and audit exceptions.

quantified_impact.metric: Sections naming a different receipt signer

risks.severity_reason: The wording is ambiguous for every shipped purchase, and the gap shows up at reconciliation and audit.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The signed paper SOA sits between the cardholder and the AO and misses the 10-workday AO certification deadline.
risks.cause: 6.C.1 gives the cardholder 7 workdays and 6.C.2 gives the AO 10 workdays from the same cycle end. The paper SOA passes by hand with no tracking.
risks.impact: Late certification, late payment to the bank, and possible suspension for untimely reconciliation (11.B).

quantified_impact.basis: Map handoffs after S35 and S38

risks.severity_reason: This runs monthly for every cardholder with a 3-workday window, and lateness triggers sanctions.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The cardholder has to chase another employee for a signature on the invoice and cannot reconcile until it arrives, so the 7-workday deadline slips.
risks.cause: 6.C.3 states the cardholder 'may not reconcile... until' the other employee signs and dates the invoice. No routing or deadline is given for that employee.
risks.impact: Late reconciliation and a knock-on delay to AO certification.
risks.severity_reason: It applies only when goods go to someone else, but it blocks the whole SOA when it does.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: Transaction data already on the bank SOA is typed again into the core financial accounting system, and keying errors post charges to the wrong accounts.
risks.cause: 7.B makes the CFO responsible for 'ensuring all reconciled purchase card transaction data is entered' into the core system from SOAs forwarded on paper (6.C.2).
risks.impact: Wrong charge distribution and extra work to correct accounts.

quantified_impact.basis: Data on the bank SOA (S31) re-entered at S39

risks.severity_reason: Re-entry happens every cycle, and errors affect budget accuracy but can be corrected.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: Cardholders destroy records too early because one section counts six years from the purchase and another from final payment.
risks.cause: 6.D says retain 'for a period of six (6) years', while 7.F.9 says 'six (6) years after final payment'.
risks.impact: Records may be unavailable for audit or investigation.
risks.severity_reason: The difference is short, but it creates inconsistent disposal decisions.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The cardholder is required to keep a copy of the SOA signed by both cardholder and AO, but the AO sends the signed SOA to FOC and nothing returns a copy to the cardholder.
risks.cause: 6.D requires the cardholder to keep the SOA 'signed and dated by the cardholder and the AO'. 6.C.2 and 7.E.4 send the AO-signed SOA to FOC with no copy back.
risks.impact: Purchase files lack the fully signed SOA, which leads to APC standing reviews under 6.D.

quantified_impact.metric: Steps that return a signed copy to the cardholder
quantified_impact.basis: No step after S38 in the map routes to the cardholder

risks.severity_reason: This affects every SOA, and missing documents are an explicit trigger for suspension review.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The cardholder's AO is on leave during the 3-workday review window, and no one else can certify the SOA.
risks.cause: 6.C.2 and 7.E.4 assign review to the cardholder's AO. 14.B provides a replacement only when the AO separates or transfers, not for absences.
risks.impact: Missed 10-workday deadline and delayed payment.
risks.severity_reason: Absences are routine, and the window is short.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A cardholder spends weeks trying to resolve a charge with the merchant and passes the 90-day bank dispute window, so the government pays an improper charge.
risks.cause: 12.A sets a 90-calendar-day limit from when the charge first appeared and says 'Cardholders shall track disputes to completion'. No log, reminder or AO visibility is stated.
risks.impact: Loss of dispute rights, payment of improper charges, and possible disciplinary action for the cardholder.
risks.severity_reason: Merchant follow-up often drags, and a missed window is unrecoverable.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A merchant refuses to credit a shipping or tax charge, or the bank denies a dispute, and the cardholder has no stated next step.
risks.cause: 12.B says shipping and tax disputes can only be resolved with the merchant but gives no path if the merchant refuses. 12.A gives no handling for a denied bank dispute.
risks.impact: Improper charges stay on the account with no escalation or documented closure.

quantified_impact.basis: D18 shipping/tax branch UNDEFINED; S45 bank denial exception has no handling

risks.severity_reason: It happens occasionally, and the cost is a lost credit plus an unclear audit trail.

risks.process: Report a lost or stolen card
risks.what_could_go_wrong: The cardholder calls the bank but forgets to tell the AO or APC. Nobody checks for fraudulent charges, and no replacement is arranged.
risks.cause: Section 13 and 7.F.3 require three separate 'immediate' notifications but state no follow-up by the APC or AO after notice.
risks.impact: Fraudulent charges may go unnoticed until reconciliation, and the cardholder has no card.
risks.severity_reason: It is infrequent, but the exposure is direct financial loss.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: Form A-498 circulates between nominee, Bureau/Office Chief and AO for signatures and gets lost or delayed before the package reaches FOC.
risks.cause: 6.A.3 and 7.F.1 require a nominee-signed form also signed by the Chief and the AO, then submitted with the application to FOC RDG/TOG. The D2 'No' branch has no next step.
risks.impact: Delayed card issuance for the requester.

quantified_impact.metric: Handoffs for Form A-498 and package
quantified_impact.basis: Map handoffs after S3, S4, S5 and S7

risks.severity_reason: Every issuance passes through this chain, but the impact is delay rather than loss.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The cardholder's training certificate goes to FOC RDG/TOG with the application but not to the APC, and the APC cannot confirm training before issuing the card.
risks.cause: 6.A.4 says certificates 'must be submitted to the APC prior to issuance', while 7.F.1 says to submit the certificate with the bank application to FOC RDG/TOG.
risks.impact: Card issued without verified training, or issuance held up.
risks.severity_reason: Both recipients sit in Financial Operations, so the confusion is likely but usually resolved.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A temporary credit limit increase is never reversed because no step returns the limit to its original level. Separately, a permanent request from outside OMD has no stated outcome.
risks.cause: 6.B.4 requires the APC to retain the length of time for an increase but states no reversal step. D5 'Yes' has no next step.
risks.impact: Higher spending exposure than intended and unclear answers for requesting AOs.

quantified_impact.metric: Steps to reverse a temporary increase
quantified_impact.basis: No such step in 6.B.4 or the map

risks.severity_reason: It is likely over time, and a lingering higher limit weakens a key spending control.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: Permanent limit increases are never re-reviewed because 'periodic' has no defined interval, and when a limit is no longer needed there is no stated action.
risks.cause: 6.B.5 says 'on a periodic basis' with no interval, and the D6 'No' branch is undefined.
risks.impact: Unneeded high limits remain in place.
risks.severity_reason: Only permanent OMD increases are affected, and the exposure grows slowly.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A departing cardholder's account stays open because the APC, the only role that closes accounts, is unavailable or misses the notice.
risks.cause: 14.C and 7.D assign account closure and card destruction to the APC, with no backup named.
risks.impact: An open card for a departed employee and risk of unauthorized charges.

quantified_impact.metric: Roles able to close an account

risks.severity_reason: It is unlikely in any one case, but the exposure is an active card with no owner.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The cardholder, the AO and the Bureau/Office Chief each assume someone else told the APC about the departure, so no notice arrives before the person leaves.
risks.cause: 7.F.10 has the cardholder notify the APC. 14.A says notice is given by the AO or Bureau/Office Chief. 7.E.8 has the AO direct cancellation. 7.C.9 has Chiefs report status changes.
risks.impact: The account stays open after departure, and records are not collected.
risks.severity_reason: Diffused ownership makes a miss likely, and an open card for a departed employee is a direct misuse exposure.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A departing cardholder waits for account cancellation before handing over records, leaves first, and the files are lost.
risks.cause: 14.A requires records 'promptly (and before separation or transfer)'. 7.F.11 says to transfer them 'upon cancellation of the account, or separation'. 7.F.11 also requires files to stay available after departure.
risks.impact: Records cannot be produced for audits within the 6-year retention period.
risks.severity_reason: Departures are routine, and lost files are an audit finding.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: Bureaus/Offices sit on the inactive-account list because no deadline or named responder is set, and accounts reported as no longer needed have no closure step.
risks.cause: 6.A.5 requires the Bureau/Office to confirm but names no person or deadline, and gives no handling for accounts not needed.
risks.impact: Unneeded accounts stay open or are suspended without clear follow-up.
risks.severity_reason: It is infrequent and limited to dormant accounts.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A cardholder's 3-year refresher lapses unnoticed because nothing reminds them or flags the lapse.
risks.cause: 6.A.4 requires refresher training every three years, but no reminder, due-date tracking or lapse handling is stated.
risks.impact: Untrained cardholders keep purchasing, which is an audit finding.
risks.severity_reason: Lapses are likely over a long cycle, but the immediate financial exposure is low.

risks.process: Respond to a purchase card review or audit
risks.what_could_go_wrong: An auditor's document request goes unanswered for weeks because 'timely' is undefined and the cardholder's files are scattered.
risks.cause: 6.E.1 requires documents 'in a timely manner' with no period, and 6.E.2 makes the cardholder personally responsible even if files are centralized.
risks.impact: Audit findings and APC standing review (6.D) that can lead to suspension.
risks.severity_reason: Reviews are periodic or random, and failure has direct consequences for the cardholder.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: An AO leaves before a replacement is named, so cardholders cannot get purchase authorizations and SOAs miss the 10-workday certification.
risks.cause: 14.B requires a new AO to be designated and sent in writing to the APC but sets no deadline.
risks.impact: Purchasing stops for the affected cardholders, and certification is late.
risks.severity_reason: AO turnover is occasional, but it blocks every cardholder under that AO.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: After an OIG investigation where no disciplinary action is proposed, the case has no closure step. Suspended privileges have no clear test for restoration.
risks.cause: 11.E gives no path when no action is proposed (D23 'No'), and 11.B restores privileges only 'until compliance is observed' without criteria.
risks.impact: Cases stay open indefinitely, and restoration decisions are inconsistent.
risks.severity_reason: It is rare, and these are sensitive personnel decisions that must stay human.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The nominee completes Form A-498 in a Power Apps form with an electronic certification checkbox and uploads the GSA training certificate, writing to a SharePoint 'Card Nominations' list.
recommendations.reason: A paper form with three signatures is easy to lose. One digital record also captures the training certificate needed before issuance (6.A.3, 6.A.4).
implementation_steps: Create SharePoint list 'Card Nominations' with nominee, role (cardholder/AO), Bureau/Office, Chief, AO, certification flag and status columns.
Add a document library for training certificates linked by nomination ID.
Build a Power Apps form replicating Form A-498 fields and the certification statement; require the certificate upload.
Confirm with FOC and OGC that electronic certification satisfies the A-498 signature requirement.

impact.basis: Estimate: removes printing, scanning and searching for the form; handoffs remain but become tracked.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When a nomination is submitted, a flow sends sequential approval requests to the Bureau/Office Chief (or ABC) and then the AO, recording names and timestamps.
recommendations.reason: These are rule-based signature routings (7.F.1) that currently move by hand.
implementation_steps: Trigger a Power Automate flow on new item in 'Card Nominations'.
Start an approval to the Bureau/Office Chief; on approval, start an approval to the named AO.
Write approver names, dates and outcomes back to the list and set the status.
On rejection, notify the nominee and the requester with comments.

impact.basis: Estimate: the 2 signature handoffs (after S3, S4) become tracked approvals instead of carried paper.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: After both approvals, a flow assembles the signed A-498 PDF, training certificate and bank application and sends one package to FOC RDG/TOG and the APC.
recommendations.reason: This removes the manual package submission and satisfies both 6.A.4 (to the APC) and 7.F.1 (to FOC).
implementation_steps: Add bank application fields or an attachment to the nomination form.
In the approval flow, generate a PDF of the approved A-498 from a Word template.
Email the PDF, certificate and application to the FOC RDG/TOG shared mailbox and the APC.
Set the nomination status to 'Submitted to FOC'.

impact.basis: Estimate: the nominee no longer assembles and sends the package; the S7 handoff becomes automatic.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The APC continues to judge each justification case by case.
recommendations.reason: 6.B.1 requires a case-by-case judgment of demonstrated need, which is a control decision.
implementation_steps: No automation; the APC records the decision in the cardholder register for traceability.

impact.basis: keep_human; no change

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The AO submits Form A-1204 in a Power Apps form, recording circumstances, temporary or permanent, and an end date for temporary increases.
recommendations.reason: This captures the data the APC must retain (6.B.4) at the source.
implementation_steps: Create SharePoint list 'Credit Limit Requests' with cardholder, AO, Bureau/Office, current and requested limit, type, end date and justification.
Build a Power Apps form mirroring Form A-1204; make the end date required when the type is temporary.
Warn when a permanent request is for a cardholder outside OMD (6.B.4).

impact.basis: Estimate: removes paper form handling.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: A flow records the APC decision and duration automatically from the A-1204 item and reminds the APC when a temporary increase reaches its end date.
recommendations.reason: Retention becomes automatic, and temporary increases have no reversal step today.
implementation_steps: Add APC decision columns to 'Credit Limit Requests'.
Create a Power Automate approval to the APC on new request; write the outcome to the list.
Create a daily scheduled flow that finds temporary increases ending within 5 days and emails the APC to restore the limit.
Log the APC's confirmation of reversal on the item.

impact.basis: The APC's separate record of circumstances and duration (S16) is captured from the form, removing 1 manual record. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: A scheduled flow sends the APC the list of permanent increases at an interval the program owner sets and records the 'still required' determination.
recommendations.reason: 6.B.5 sets no interval, so a scheduled trigger makes the review happen.
implementation_steps: Have the program owner set the review interval (for example, annually).
Create a Recurrence flow that queries permanent increases in 'Credit Limit Requests'.
Send an approval per item to the APC with a 'still required' choice.
Record outcomes; route 'not required' items back to the APC as a task to lower the limit.

impact.basis: Estimate: removes compiling the list of permanent increases by hand.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The cardholder submits each purchase request in a Power Apps form to a SharePoint 'Purchase Requests' list. The form captures item, merchant, amount, funding document reference, Section 508 flag, shipping and vendor terms.
recommendations.reason: This gives every transaction a single traceable record that 6.D requires (funding reference, advance authorization).
implementation_steps: Create SharePoint list 'Purchase Requests' and a document library 'Purchase Files' with one folder per request.
Build a Power Apps form with required fields: funding document reference (MOC, TG), amount, merchant, description, IT/508 flag and terms attachment.
Add a cardholder register list holding each cardholder's AO and single transaction limit, used as a lookup.
Publish the app to cardholders in Teams.

impact.basis: Estimate: replaces composing a memo or email and filing it later.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: Submitting a request starts an approval to the cardholder's AO. The AO's approve or reject decision, name and timestamp are stored as the written authorization in the purchase file.
recommendations.reason: 7.E.2 accepts email-level written authorization, so a recorded approval meets it and is retrievable for audit.
implementation_steps: Trigger a flow when an item is created in 'Purchase Requests'.
Look up the AO from the cardholder register.
Start an approval with the request details; on approve, set the status to 'Authorized' and save the approval record as PDF in the purchase folder.
On reject, set the status to 'Not authorized', notify the cardholder with comments and close the request (defines the D7 'No' branch).

impact.basis: Estimate: the 2 handoffs (after S18, S19) remain but are tracked, and the authorization is filed automatically.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The Section 508 Determination and Findings form becomes a conditional section of the purchase request form, shown when the IT flag is set.
recommendations.reason: It attaches the 508 determination to the transaction record automatically.
implementation_steps: Add Section 508 D&F fields to the Power Apps form, visible only when the IT/508 flag is Yes.
Make the fields required when visible.
Store the completed D&F as a PDF in the purchase folder via the request flow.

impact.basis: Estimate: removes separate form handling.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The request flow checks the amount against the cardholder's single transaction limit and flags possible split purchases to the AO. The cardholder still judges price reasonableness.
recommendations.reason: The limit check is rule-based (6.B.2). Splitting is named non-compliance (11.B) but is otherwise caught only at review.
implementation_steps: In the request flow, compare the amount with the limit from the cardholder register; if over, reject and tell the cardholder to seek EAC or a limit increase.
Query 'Purchase Requests' for the same cardholder and merchant within a set window (owner-defined, for example 7 days) where the combined amount exceeds the limit.
Add a 'possible split' warning to the AO approval card when found.
Keep a required cardholder attestation field 'price considered reasonable'.

impact.basis: Estimate: an automatic check replaces a manual limit lookup.

recommendations.label: ai_assist
recommendations.proposed_change: An AI Builder prompt reads the uploaded vendor terms and highlights clauses that look like recurring payments, auto-renewal, unlimited duration, indemnification or unlimited liability. The cardholder confirms the result.
recommendations.reason: Long online terms are hard to scan, and 6.A.8 lists clear categories to classify against.
implementation_steps: Require a terms attachment (or pasted text) on requests where terms apply.
Create an AI Builder custom prompt that returns found categories with quoted clauses.
Call the prompt from the request flow and write the results to the item and the AO approval card.
Require the cardholder to confirm or override the flags; never auto-clear a request.
recommendations.suggested_tool: AI Builder (custom prompt) in Power Automate

impact.basis: Estimate of reading time saved; human confirmation remains.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When prohibited provisions are confirmed, the flow holds the request and routes it with the terms to an EAC queue before any commitment.
recommendations.reason: 6.A.8 requires referral to EAC before commitment, and automatic routing prevents a skipped referral.
implementation_steps: Add status 'Referred to EAC' and an EAC assignee column.
When the prohibited-terms flag is confirmed, set the status and post to the EAC Teams channel or shared mailbox with a link.
Block the AO 'Authorized' status until EAC records an outcome (contract established, or forgo vendor).

impact.basis: Estimate: the S25 handoff becomes tracked.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: EAC continues to establish contracts addressing objectionable terms, consulting OGC as needed.
recommendations.reason: Contract and legal judgment (6.A.8).
implementation_steps: No automation; EAC records the outcome on the request item.

impact.basis: keep_human; no change

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: Receipt of goods is confirmed in the app on the purchase request: upload a photo or PDF of the receipt or invoice and record the receiver and date.
recommendations.reason: It defines one recorded receipt confirmation for the purchase file (7.E.3, 6.D).
implementation_steps: Add a 'Confirm receipt' screen to the Power Apps app with an invoice upload and receiver name and date.
Have the program owner decide who confirms receipt (AO, accepting employee or purchaser), resolving the wording conflict across 7.E.3, 6.C.3 and 6.D.
Save the invoice to the purchase folder and set the status to 'Received'.

impact.basis: Estimate: removes paper invoice signing and filing.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When goods go to another employee, a flow sends that employee an acceptance request and records the signature and date on the invoice record.
recommendations.reason: 6.C.3 blocks reconciliation until this signature exists, and chasing it by hand delays the 7-workday deadline.
implementation_steps: Add an 'Accepting employee' person field to 'Purchase Requests'.
On status 'Received', start an approval to the accepting employee with the invoice attached.
Record the response and timestamp, and stamp the invoice PDF with the acceptance details.
Remind the employee daily until answered and alert the cardholder at 5 workdays after cycle end.

impact.occurrence: per invoice accepted by another employee
impact.basis: Estimate of chase time saved.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The cardholder uploads the bank's transaction export, and a flow matches each line to authorized purchase requests and flags unmatched or third-party-processor lines for review.
recommendations.reason: Matching SOA lines to purchases is repeatable. Third-party processor names make it error-prone (6.D).
implementation_steps: Confirm the contractor bank portal can export transactions as CSV or Excel.
Create a SharePoint library 'SOA Uploads'; trigger a flow on file upload.
Parse rows (Excel Online connector) and match on amount, date window and merchant to 'Purchase Requests'.
Write a match status per line and list unmatched lines for the cardholder; the cardholder resolves exceptions manually.

impact.basis: Estimate. Effort is 4 because no standard bank connector is known and the export format must be confirmed.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The cardholder records any Certification Clause exceptions and certifies the reconciled SOA in the app. The SOA is routed to the AO as a tracked approval, with reminders before the 10-workday deadline and escalation to the Bureau/Office Chief.
recommendations.reason: The paper SOA handoff has only a 3-workday window (6.C.1, 6.C.2).
implementation_steps: Create SharePoint list 'SOA Certifications' (cardholder, cycle end, SOA PDF, exceptions text, cardholder certification timestamp).
Add an app screen for exceptions (initialed and dated via user and timestamp) and certification with the 6.C.4 clause text.
On certification, start an approval to the AO with the SOA PDF; send a reminder at workday 8 and escalate to the Bureau/Office Chief at workday 9.
Confirm with FOC and OGC that electronic signature with printed name and date meets 6.C.1; otherwise use an e-signature connector.

impact.basis: Estimate: removes printing, signing and hand delivery; the S35 handoff becomes tracked.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The AO still personally reviews each transaction for legality, propriety and necessity.
recommendations.reason: This is a certification with legal accountability (6.C.4, 7.E.4).
implementation_steps: No automation of the judgment; the AO reviews within the approval created by A18.

impact.basis: keep_human; no change

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The AO records exceptions and certifies in the approval. A flow then generates the dual-certified SOA PDF, sends it to FOC RDG/TOG and saves a copy in the cardholder's purchase file.
recommendations.reason: It removes the manual forward and closes the gap where the cardholder never receives the fully signed copy (6.D vs 6.C.2).
implementation_steps: On AO approval, write the AO name, date and exceptions to 'SOA Certifications'.
Generate a PDF combining the SOA with both certifications (Word template or Adobe connector).
Email or post it to the FOC RDG/TOG shared mailbox or library, and save a copy to the cardholder's 'Purchase Files' folder.
Mark the cycle 'Certified' for CFO timeliness reporting (7.B).

impact.basis: Estimate: the S38 handoff becomes automatic and the copy is filed.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: Certified transactions with their funding references are exported in a structured file for FOC to upload into the core financial accounting system instead of retyping.
recommendations.reason: It removes re-entry of SOA data (7.B).
implementation_steps: Confirm with FOC the import format the core financial system accepts.
Build a flow that, on certification, writes matched transactions with funding codes to an Excel or CSV file in an FOC library.
FOC uploads the file through the system's import function and records the upload date.
Add a reconciliation check comparing the file total to the SOA total.

impact.basis: Removes 1 re-entry of SOA data per transaction (S31 data re-keyed at S39). Minutes are an estimate. Effort is 4 because the core system integration is unknown.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: Purchase files (authorization, invoices, 508 D&F, certified SOA) live in a SharePoint library per cardholder with a 6-year retention label, so the cardholder can share them directly with reviewers.
recommendations.reason: It centralizes the 6.D documentation (allowed by 6.E.2) and applies retention consistently.
implementation_steps: Have the program owner resolve the 6.D vs 7.F.9 retention anchor (from purchase or from final payment).
Create a Purview retention label of 6 years based on the chosen event, and apply it to the 'Purchase Files' library.
Structure folders by cardholder and request; grant the cardholder, AO and APC access.
Provide a 'share with reviewer' view per cycle so the cardholder can furnish documents quickly.

impact.basis: Estimate of filing and retrieval time saved.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The cardholder logs each dispute in a SharePoint 'Disputes' list with the date the charge first appeared on the SOA, the charge type, merchant contacts and outcome.
recommendations.reason: 12.A requires documented merchant actions, and the first-appeared date drives the 90-day limit.
implementation_steps: Create list 'Disputes' with transaction, first-appeared date, charge type (shipping/tax or other), merchant contact log, bank dispute date, status and outcome.
Add a dispute screen to the Power Apps app.
Flag shipping and tax disputes as merchant-only (12.B).
Have the program owner define handling for merchant refusal and bank denial, and add those statuses.

impact.basis: Estimate of documentation time saved.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: A flow calculates the 90-day deadline from the first-appeared date and reminds the cardholder and AO until the dispute is filed and closed.
recommendations.reason: Missing the 90-day window is unrecoverable (12.A).
implementation_steps: Add a calculated deadline column (first-appeared date + 90 calendar days).
Create a daily Recurrence flow that finds open disputes not yet filed with the bank.
Email the cardholder at 30, 60 and 80 days, and copy the AO at 80 days (7.E.6 AO assists).
Post a weekly open-dispute summary to the cardholder until status is 'Closed'.

impact.basis: Estimate: removes manual deadline tracking.

recommendations.process: Report a lost or stolen card
recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: After calling the bank, the cardholder submits one 'lost or stolen card' report in the app, which notifies the AO and APC at once and logs the bank report time.
recommendations.reason: Section 13 requires immediate notice to two internal parties, and one action prevents a missed notice.
implementation_steps: Add a 'Report lost or stolen card' screen capturing date, bank reference number and circumstances.
Trigger a flow that emails and Teams-messages the AO and APC with high importance.
Create a follow-up task for the APC (planner or list item) to confirm cancellation and review recent charges.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Apps + Power Automate (Outlook, Teams, Planner)

impact.basis: Estimate: two separate notifications become one submission.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: A scheduled flow reads each cardholder's and AO's last training date and reminds them before the 3-year due date, copying the APC on overdue items.
recommendations.reason: The 3-year cycle is rule-based (6.A.4).
implementation_steps: Add last training date and due date columns to the cardholder register.
Create a weekly Recurrence flow that emails people due within 60 days.
Send the APC a list of overdue cardholders and AOs.

impact.occurrence: per refresher cycle per cardholder or AO
impact.basis: Estimate of APC tracking time saved.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: Cardholders and AOs upload the refresher certificate through the app, which updates their training date in the register.
recommendations.reason: Certificates must be available on request (7.F.2) and are currently sent ad hoc.
implementation_steps: Add a certificate upload screen to the app saving to a 'Training Certificates' library.
On upload, a flow updates the last training date in the cardholder register and notifies the APC.

impact.basis: Estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The APC loads the inactive-account list, and a flow sends each Bureau/Office contact an approval per account with a response due date and records the confirmations.
recommendations.reason: 6.A.5 sets no deadline or responder, and tracked approvals make non-response visible.
implementation_steps: Create list 'Inactive Account Review' with account, Bureau/Office, contact and response.
Have the program owner set a response deadline and named contact per Bureau/Office.
Start approvals ('continue' or 'not needed') to each contact and send a reminder before the deadline.
Give the APC a list of non-responses (suspend) and 'not needed' accounts (close).

impact.occurrence: per inactive account per review cycle
impact.basis: Estimate.

recommendations.process: Respond to a purchase card review or audit
recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The APC continues to decide the cardholder's standing after missing documentation.
recommendations.reason: This is a sanction decision about a person (6.D).
implementation_steps: No automation.

impact.basis: keep_human; no change

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: Suspension or revocation remains an APC decision.
recommendations.reason: This is a sensitive personnel and control decision (11.B).
implementation_steps: No automation.

impact.basis: keep_human; no change

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: Disciplinary or adverse actions continue to follow the HR progression.
recommendations.reason: These are legal and labor-relations decisions (11.E).
implementation_steps: No automation.

impact.basis: keep_human; no change

recommendations.label: eliminate
recommendations.proposed_change: The cardholder's separate notice to the APC is replaced by the single separation notice in A33. The cardholder can start that notice and is copied on it.
recommendations.reason: Four sections assign the same notice, and one tracked notice removes the duplicate. The program owner must amend 7.F.10 accordingly.
implementation_steps: Program owner amends 7.F.10 to point to the single separation notice.
Let cardholders start the separation form in A33; the AO or Chief completes it.

impact.basis: Removes step S65 and its Cardholder-to-APC handoff. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The AO or Bureau/Office Chief submits one separation or transfer notice in the app. It notifies the APC (shared mailbox) and creates a tracked checklist: records handover, card surrender, account closure and final SOA note.
recommendations.reason: It clarifies a single owner and gives APC backup staff visibility of pending closures.
implementation_steps: Create list 'Separations' with cardholder, effective date, submitter and checklist status columns.
Build a Power Apps form that the cardholder can start and the AO or Chief must submit.
On submit, email the APC shared mailbox and create checklist items with due dates before the effective date.
Send a daily reminder to the APC and AO for open items past the effective date.

impact.basis: Estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When the separation notice is submitted, a flow grants the AO ownership of the cardholder's SharePoint purchase file folder before the effective date.
recommendations.reason: Records already live in SharePoint (A22), so the handover becomes a permission change, and files stay available after departure (7.F.11).
implementation_steps: Have the program owner set the handover timing as before separation (14.A) and align 7.F.11.
In the separation flow, use SharePoint HTTP actions to grant the AO full control of the cardholder's folder.
Ask the cardholder to confirm all paper records are scanned in, as a checklist item.
Remove the cardholder's access after the effective date.

impact.basis: Estimate. Effort is 3 because it uses SharePoint REST permission calls.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The Chief submits the new AO designation in the app. It updates the AO on each cardholder in the register (so approvals route to the new AO) and notifies the APC in writing.
recommendations.reason: It keeps purchase authorizations and SOA certifications flowing during AO turnover.
implementation_steps: Add an 'AO designation' form to the app (old AO, new AO, effective date).
On submit, a flow updates the AO field for affected cardholders in the register and emails the APC.
Have the program owner set a designation deadline relative to the AO's departure, and send a reminder when an AO separation notice exists without a designation.

impact.basis: Estimate.

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint: When an item is created in 'Purchase Requests' (submitted from the Power Apps purchase request form)
actions: Get the cardholder's record (AO, single transaction limit) from the cardholder register list
Condition: funding document reference is empty; if yes, update the item status to 'Incomplete' and email the cardholder
Create a folder in the 'Purchase Files' library named with the request ID
Copy the form attachments (vendor terms, quotes, 508 D&F) into the folder
Update the item status to 'Awaiting AO authorization' and store the folder link
Hand off to the authorization flow (A9) by setting the status that triggers it

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint: When an item is modified in 'Purchase Requests' and its status equals 'Awaiting AO authorization'
actions: Get the AO from the cardholder register
Compose an approval summary: item, merchant, amount, funding reference, 508 flag, possible-split and terms flags
Start and wait for an approval (Approve/Reject) assigned to the AO
If approved: update the status to 'Authorized', and write the AO name, response date and comments to the item
Create an authorization record PDF from a Word template and save it in the purchase folder
If rejected: update the status to 'Not authorized' and email the cardholder the AO comments
If there is no response within 2 workdays: send a reminder to the AO
starter_flows.approval_step: AO approves or rejects the purchase before it is made (7.E.2). The approval record with name and timestamp serves as the written authorization.

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint: When an item is created in 'SOA Certifications' (cardholder certifies the reconciled SOA in Power Apps)
actions: Get the cardholder's AO and the billing cycle end date
Calculate workday 10 after cycle end (excluding weekends and a holiday list)
Start an approval to the AO with the SOA PDF, matched transactions and cardholder exceptions
Run in parallel: a delay until workday 8, then email a reminder to the AO if still pending
Run in parallel: a delay until workday 9, then email the Bureau/Office Chief if still pending
On AO response: write the AO decision, name, date and exceptions to the item
Hand off to A20 to generate the certified PDF, send it to FOC RDG/TOG and file a copy in the cardholder's purchase file
starter_flows.approval_step: AO reviews and certifies the reconciled SOA within 10 workdays of cycle end (6.C.2), noting any Certification Clause exceptions.
